findings.finding: Windows arm's spawnSync had no maxBuffer (asymmetric with the POSIX fix applied 20 lines below), and dropping the Where-Object clause increased pipe volume.

filterTsxEntriesByRepo's trailing-boundary anchor does not also anchor the leading edge, so a repoRoot that recurs verbatim as a subpath of a different absolute path (e.g. a POSIX bind mount) could still false-match.

Claim under doubt: scoping the tsx sweep to this checkout makes the deploy strictly better-behaved toward other checkouts — The two sweeps are now ASYMMETRIC. stopOldServer still runs findListenerPids(port) machine-wide and kills whatever holds the port, from ANY checkout — only the PARENT sweep became repo-scoped. When a sibling worktree's tsx watch holds the deploy's port (CLAUDE.md documents this as the usual EADDRINUSE cause), the deploy kills that foreign dev server's child and spares its parent.

Claim under doubt: the sweep still reliably catches the tsx watch PARENT on a real production deploy — findTsxServerPids() returned [] identically for 4 different states: nothing running, discovery failed (PowerShell/CIM error), candidates existed but none matched this repo, or genuine zero — with zero signal anywhere to distinguish them.

Claim under doubt: the kill sequence ends the watch parent before it can matter — killed was built listener-PIDs first, tsx-PIDs second, and killed in that order — so the watch CHILD (the listener) was killed BEFORE its parent, risking a respawn race.

Claim under doubt: repoRoot: serverDir identifies this checkout's processes reliably — It is a text match, not a realpath — a symlinked/junctioned/subst checkout could present a different spelling on each side and silently under-match.

Claim under doubt: the fix is protected by tests against future regression — deploy-tsx-scope.test.js (node --test) is not wired into CI — only server/client vitest runs there, so the behavioral guard never executes on a PR; only the source-regex contract test does.

Claim under doubt: the synthetic fixtures prove the Windows arm works on a real host — The PowerShell invocation changed shape in this diff and is only exercised via hand-built JSON fixtures, never against a real host; a non-ASCII byte or BOM in the redirected stdout could corrupt the JSON stream.

Claim under doubt: once stopOldServer reports freed: true, the port is ours — freed: true is a single-poll observation with no re-confirmation; a respawned foreign parent could still win the port after we observe it free.
Claim under doubt: this iterate improved kill precision end-to-end — The kill itself (taskkill/SIGTERM by PID) has no re-validation against PID reuse in the enumeration window.

Claim under doubt: 'a tsx watch command line always embeds node_modules/tsx/...' is a stable contract — That is an undocumented implementation detail of tsx's argv formatting; a minor tsx version bump moving loader flags out of argv would defeat the match silently.

repoRoot` is matched as-given text, not canonicalized. If the deploy is run from a path reached via symlink, `subst` drive, or a differently-cased spelling than what's embedded in the dev server's argv (the dev server may have been started from the other spelling), the pattern silently under-matches, the watch parent survives, and the port is blocked — with the diagnostic reporting `matched: 0` but no way to distinguish this from "nothing running". The code documents this, but the operator-facing `onDiag` output in deploy-swap.mjs doesn't hint at it.
findings.suggestion: Consider a `fs.realpathSync(serverDir)` (guarded by try/catch) at the deploy-swap call site, or mention path-spelling mismatch in the `foreignHint` text when `raw > 0 && matched === 0`.

findings.finding: On Windows, a repoRoot containing a space is fine (the root itself is matched literally), but the `(?:[^\s"']+/)` gap between `node_modules/` and `tsx/` cannot cross a space, and a quoted tsx path whose intermediate segments contain spaces would fail to match. This is unreachable for the standard `.bin/../tsx/` npm shim hop, so it's theoretical only.
findings.suggestion: None needed; note it alongside the existing residual documentation if you want completeness.

findings.finding: /src[\\/]index\.ts/i` also matches `src/index.tsx` (no trailing boundary). This is inherited verbatim from the pre-fix match, not a regression, and over-matching here only widens the candidate set before repo-scoping — the repo filter still constrains the kill set.
findings.suggestion: Optional: add a `(?![a-z])` lookahead if you want the marker tightened.

findings.finding: The comment-stripping filter only handles `` and `//` line prefixes; a `pgrep -a` embedded mid-line in code or in a `/ /` span would slip past. Low stakes since it's a cheap pin with behavioral coverage elsewhere, and the current source passes it correctly.
findings.suggestion: Strip `/ ... /` spans before scanning, or accept as-is.

findings.finding: Repo ownership is inferred from a match anywhere in the flattened command line. A foreign worktree’s `tsx watch src/index.ts` process that includes `--import <deploying-server>/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs` will be selected and killed, even though its own `tsx` executable resolves from the foreign worktree. This directly violates the required cross-worktree isolation.
findings.suggestion: Identify the executable/loader that owns the process rather than accepting an arbitrary matching argument; alternatively use reliable process cwd/parent ownership data. Add a fixture for a repo-B tsx invocation with a repo-A `--import .../node_modules/tsx/...` argument and assert it is excluded.

findings.finding: The regex has no leading path boundary. On POSIX, deploying `/home/dev/app/server` will also match a different checkout invoked from `/mnt/archive/home/dev/app/server/node_modules/tsx/...`, because the target root appears as a suffix of that foreign absolute path. The code comments acknowledge this, but it remains an unwanted process kill contrary to the acceptance criteria.
findings.suggestion: Require a valid argv/path boundary before the normalized repo root, or use resolved process ownership/cwd rather than substring matching.

findings.finding: The “incidental argument” test only uses a `dotenv` path, while the implementation specifically accepts foreign arguments containing `<repoRoot>/node_modules/.../tsx/`. Thus the tests pass despite the concrete cross-worktree kill defect above.
findings.suggestion: Add negative cases for foreign `--import`/`--require` arguments referencing the deploying checkout’s `tsx` package and for a POSIX path containing the target repo root as a suffix.  Overall: ship-with-fixes. The normal scoped path works, but the matcher still permits concrete false positives that can kill an unrelated worktree’s dev server.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
